solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Decreasing support for an alternative to 28?

definitions.text: Decreasing support for an alternative to 28?

parts.words: Decreasing support for an alternative to 28?
parts.note: read 'decreasing' as de-creasing, taking creases out; the item that holds clothes while that happens is the alternative to the press at 28

explanation.surface: Something lowering support in a debate is offered as a substitute for some other item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decreasing' looks like 'reducing', but here it means removing creases. 28 is TROUSER PRESS, another way of getting creases out of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat padded stand you iron clothes on supports them while their creases are pressed out.

clue.text: Brilliant Sky display — Egghead gets unlimited whiskey

indicators.note: without its limits, so the word brainbox loses its first and last letters

parts.note: an egghead is a clever person, a brainbox
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A clever TV personality on Sky, the British broadcaster, is rewarded with a bottle of whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips BRAINBOX to RAINBO; W for whiskey finishes it. 'Sky' is capitalised to suggest the TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc of brilliant colours seen in the sky after rain is the classic dazzling natural display.

clue.text: American Conservative supporting gun reform is futile

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits below, so the gun letters come first and the rest follows
to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters of gun are rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A right-wing American politician backs firearms legislation, which proves pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' turns GUN into NUG; in a down clue 'supporting' puts A and TORY underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory is a formal word for something of no value or effect, so it is a synonym of useless or futile.

clue.text: Number regularly sampling Indian tea?

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of Indian tea

explanation.surface: A question about how many cups of Indian tea someone tries in a tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cardinal figure, the one after eight, so it is an example of a number.

clue.text: Pretty girl, British, modelling Dior label

indicators.note: modelling means shaping, so the letters of Dior label are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: An attractive British woman works as a model for the Dior fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelling' rearranges DIOR LABEL into ARBIEDOLL, after B for British.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for a conventionally attractive but vacuous young woman, after the famous toy.

clue.text: Prize runs into a lot of cash

indicators.note: the r for runs goes into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: a wad is a thick bundle of banknotes
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A prize that adds up to a large sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R (runs, as in cricket scoring) inside A WAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is something given in recognition of merit, a synonym of prize.

clue.text: Flier heading north allowed a drop

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so bird is written backwards

parts.note: a bird is a flier
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A bird flying north is allowed to drop down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'heading north' means read upwards, so the bird is turned round before 'allowed' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A driblet is a small quantity of liquid, a tiny drip, so it is a synonym of a drop.

clue.text: Fine milky coffee on northern cycling trip having finished climb

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a latte is coffee made with lots of steamed milk

indicators.note: the letters of the word for a trip go round, the front ones moving to the back

parts.note: an outing is a trip

explanation.surface: A cyclist enjoys a latte after reaching the top of a northern hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like part of the cycling scene but signals moving the front letters of the trip word to its end. The definition describes a plane levelling off after its ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft levelling off at cruising height stops gaining altitude, so it has ended its ascent.

clue.text: Tom's hoovering busily, trying to tidy up

indicators.note: working busily suggests things being moved about, so the letters of Tom's hoovering are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tom is vacuuming energetically in an effort to clean the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The domestic scene hides a figurative definition: tidying up a dispute rather than a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth things over is to settle a difficulty and make a situation seem less bad.

clue.text: Cuddly in ginormous blankets — not getting up!

indicators.note: the outer words cover the answer the way blankets cover a sleeper

explanation.surface: Someone cosy under huge blankets refuses to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blankets' is a verb here: cudLY IN GINormous wraps the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in means staying in bed later than usual in the morning, the opposite of rising.

clue.text: Country showcasing island art school

indicators.note: a showcase holds what it displays, so the country word holds the island letters

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom or country

explanation.surface: A nation puts on display the art of one of its islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is an artistic movement depicting subjects truthfully, without idealisation.

clue.text: Disputed territory tense? I'll say so!

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
'I bet!' is an exclamation of strong agreement

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a contested region is tense and is told emphatically that it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan region's sovereignty has long been contested between China and its exiled government.

clue.text: Very fashionable young man recalled, licence to kill, hot stuff!

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: called back, so lad is written backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young man
00 is the James Bond prefix meaning licensed to kill, read as the letters OO

explanation.surface: A trendy young spy, like James Bond, is remembered as being very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses LAD to DAL. James Bond's 007 code number marks a 00 agent, one with a licence to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A vindaloo is a fiercely spicy curry, so it is literally hot food.

clue.text: Books moved inch closer

indicators.note: the letters of inch closer are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shifted a little nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: Chronicles is also the name of two books of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronicles are historical records written as books, and two Bible books bear the name.

clue.text: Where daddy turned into a horrible man?

indicators.note: turning into something else is changing form, so the letters of where daddy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about where a father became a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Dr Jekyll turning into his evil other self in Stevenson's novella.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Hyde is the brutal alter ego of Dr Jekyll, a byword for a monstrous person.

clue.text: Eat out and so on, ending in lunch

parts.note: etc is short for et cetera, and so on

indicators.note: the final letter of lunch is taken

explanation.surface: Someone dines out, among other things, finishing with a lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' suggests a restaurant, but it means corrode, as acid does on a printing plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to corrode a surface with acid, so acid eats away at it.

clue.text: Flying sensation which is intangible?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a feeling everyone senses but cannot touch

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works literally for something airborne and figuratively for a mood that pervades a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally aloft, and as an idiom describing a vague general feeling that is everywhere.

clue.text: Python moved furtively when discovered

indicators.note: dis-covered, with its covering removed, so the outer letters of sidled go

parts.note: to sidle is to move stealthily, so sidled is moved furtively

explanation.surface: A snake crept along quietly when it was spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Python' is not the snake but Eric Idle of Monty Python's Flying Circus, the British comedy team.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle was a member of the Monty Python comedy troupe, so Idle is an example of a Python.

clue.text: Drunk, that chap's beginning to tango — most nimble!

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
he's is short for he is, that chap is

indicators.note: the first letter of tango is taken

explanation.surface: A tipsy man starts dancing the tango with remarkable agility.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and agile, so its superlative is the most agile.

clue.text: Constantly changing security number which I use when managing my dough

definitions.text: which I use when managing my dough

parts.note: rolling describes something that is continually renewed, like a rolling programme
a PIN is a personal identification number used for security

explanation.surface: A bank customer describes a regularly changing PIN used to handle their money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' is slang for money, which fits the banking surface, but here it is bread or pastry dough.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook uses this wooden cylinder to flatten pastry, which is literally dough.

clue.text: Dad put on dodgy syrup which was made from reeds

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part is put on top of the second

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters of syrup are rearranged

explanation.surface: A father pours some questionable syrup that came from reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges SYRUP to PYRUS, placed under PA as 'put on' requires.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Egyptian writing material was produced from the pith of a water plant's stems.

clue.text: Family doctor covering triage barking "pull yourself together!"

indicators.note: the doctor's letters cover, sitting either side of, the rest

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, the family doctor in Britain

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters of triage are mixed up

explanation.surface: A family doctor doing triage snaps at a patient to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' (barking mad) rearranges TRIAGE to ETAGRI, which GP then surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to regain control of their emotions, the same command as to compose oneself.

clue.text: Appetizing US tortilla filled with relish

indicators.note: the clue words are filled with the answer, which sits within them

explanation.surface: A tasty American tortilla stuffed with a condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relish' looks like the tortilla filling, but it is the definition: enjoyment. The answer straddles appetizinG US TOrtilla.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment or enthusiasm, a synonym of relish in its sense of zest.

clue.text: Out of bounds, ships spot underwater hazard

indicators.note: the bounds of each word are its end letters, which are removed from ships and spot

explanation.surface: Vessels straying into a forbidden area notice a submerged danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a reef or rock, but the hazard is an animal that lurks in rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus spends much time submerged in African rivers and often attacks boats.

clue.text: Breaking end off thin mast

indicators.note: the final letter is snapped off the word for thin

parts.note: spare can mean lean or thin, as in a spare frame

explanation.surface: A slender mast snaps at its top.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole used on a ship, such as a mast, yard or boom.

clue.text: Implement U-boat's first "silent running"

indicators.note: the word first, read as a selector, picks the opening letter of the submarine word before it
running suggests something in motion, so the letters of silent are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to a German submarine to begin moving quietly to avoid detection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implement' looks like a verb giving the order, but it is a noun. 'Silent running' is the submariner's term for operating quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or instrument, especially for the kitchen, so it is a synonym of implement as a noun.

clue.text: Couple that is traversing edge of Russian plain

indicators.note: the couple and that-is letters stretch across, around, the single letter

parts.note: a pair is a couple

indicators.note: the first letter of Russian, its leading edge, is taken

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Two people cross the border region of a Russian plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traversing' makes the couple-plus-that-is letters straddle the single letter from 'edge of' Russian, which happens to land inside the couple word.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open grassland, the North American kind of flat treeless plain.

clue.text: Gadget helping to make great strides?

definitions.text: Gadget helping to make great strides?

parts.words: Gadget helping to make great strides?
parts.note: strides is British slang for trousers, so this is a device that keeps them crisp

explanation.surface: A device that helps someone make great progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make great strides' means progress fast, but strides is slang for trousers; this gadget presses them.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric appliance holds trousers flat between heated panels to put creases in them.
